title: Catalan Company
capsule: The Catalan Company (Companyia Catalana) was a band of mercenaries — primarily Aragonese almogàvers, cavalry, and Turkish auxiliaries — originally recruited by Roger de Flor for the Byzantine emperor Andronikos II in 1303 to fight the Anatolian Turks. After Roger de Flor's assassination on Byzantine orders in 1305, the Company turned on the empire in a prolonged ravaging campaign through Thrace and Macedonia known as the 'Catalan Vengeance', then entered the service of Walter V of Brienne, Duke of Athens. When Walter attempted to disband and underpay them in 1311, they killed him at the Battle of the Halmyros (15 March 1311), seized the Duchy of Athens, and placed themselves under the suzerainty of the Crown of Aragon. The Company governed the duchy until the 1380s, when Navarrese and Florentine forces progressively dislodged them; their formal presence ended with Nerio I Acciaioli's capture of Athens in 1388.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Company's territorial control over the Duchy of Athens is well documented through Aragonese chancery records and Byzantine chronicles, though the exact extent of their effective control in peripheral regions is imprecise.
